title: PEP-EDIT: a web server for the 3D generation and interactive editing of complex peptides.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: There are no data files to open. I fetched the web server home page (HTTP 200, 6.5 kB of HTML), downloaded its JavaScript bundle (1.25 MB) and listed every programming interface route it calls; the monomer-library route /api/db/monomers and four other guesses all returned 404 (not found) to a plain GET, so the 324-monomer library cannot be pulled in bulk. The source-code link in the paper (gitlab.rpbs.univ-paris-diderot.fr/rpbs/pypept-api) redirects to a sign-in page. The Europe PMC supplement is 1.28 MB and contains only figures plus one 0.97 MB PDF of methods; no tables of measurements.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The claim of a 324-entry public monomer library, the pH-dependent protonation step, and the three validation anecdotes (backbone RMSD, root-mean-square deviation of atom positions, of 3.2 A, 2.2 A and 1.41 A for the starting models against reference structures including PDB entries 7F55 and 1L5G) come from the article text only; I could not retrieve the underlying structures or any table behind them.

a1_downloadable.note: No dataset is released. The data availability statement names only the interactive web server; its monomer-library endpoint 404s to a plain GET and the source-code repository redirects to a login page. Nothing to download.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: There is no label column anywhere. Any target (e.g. how far a generated 3D model sits from the experimental structure) would have to be built by running the server on sequences and matching each to a PDB entry - exactly the 'construct the label' failure.

a3_inputs_present.note: No bulk set of input sequences exists. The paper shows a handful of example BILN (Boehringer Ingelheim Line Notation) strings in figures; the monomer definitions sit in a MongoDB behind the web interface.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are stated where numbers appear (RMSD in angstroms, pH for protonation), but there are only three such numbers in the text and no table carrying them.

a5_enough_rows.note: The largest countable asset is the 324-entry monomer library (paper text; not retrievable in bulk), and validation rests on three case studies. Far below the ~1,500-row bar, and these are chemical building blocks, not labelled examples.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially laptop-scale because there is essentially nothing to load; this is not a point in the paper's favour.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be checked: the 324-monomer count could not be confirmed against any file, because no file is downloadable.

a8_label_provenance.note: The only quantity resembling a label is the deviation of a conformer generated by the tool's own distance-geometry routine from a reference structure - i.e. a number produced by the software itself, which is the circularity A8 warns about.

existing_models.name: PEP-EDIT / pyPept (rule-based 3D conformer builder from peptide line notation, the paper's own tool)
existing_models.score_and_split: No benchmark table. Three anecdotes only: backbone RMSD (root-mean-square deviation) of 3.2 A for a 10-residue head-to-tail cyclic peptide, 2.2 A for bremelanotide against PDB 7F55, and 1.41 A for cilengitide, each against one experimental structure.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: They state that force-field parameters covering the whole monomer library, and a precise evaluation of refinement protocols, remain to be developed - i.e. the generated structures need molecular-dynamics or quantum refinement to be accurate.

existing_models.name: HighFold (AlphaFold2-based predictor for cyclic peptides with head-to-tail and disulfide constraints, Briefings in Bioinformatics 2024)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported average RMSD 1.287 A (alpha-helical) and 1.478 A (beta-sheet) on a 63-structure NMR benchmark taken from AfCycDesign; search-snippet level detail only, I did not read the full paper.

existing_models.name: CREMP-trained generative conformer models (RINGER / AGDIFF-style diffusion models for macrocyclic peptides; CREMP published in Scientific Data 2024)
existing_models.score_and_split: CREMP provides 36,198 macrocyclic peptides and ~31.3 million conformers with semi-empirical energies as training data; diffusion models trained on it are reported to reproduce simulation-quality ensembles. Search-snippet level detail only.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Snippets note that high-precision structure prediction for small cyclic peptides containing non-canonical amino acids remains challenging.

backbone.name: none applicable - no training data in this paper
backbone.licence: Article is CC BY 4.0; the server's source repository is behind a login, so its code licence is unverified.

integration.partner_dataset: CREMP (36,198 macrocyclic peptides with conformer ensembles) or CycPeptMPDB (membrane-permeability measurements for cyclic peptides)
integration.join_key: peptide sequence / line notation, or InChIKey of the assembled molecule
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Those partner resources are where the actual modelling data lives; PEP-EDIT contributes only a structure-building utility to such a project, so the join would be one-sided and this paper is not the thing being evaluated in it.

controls.positive_control: None available in this paper - no held-out measurements exist.
controls.external_validation: Experimental cyclic-peptide structures in the PDB (e.g. 7F55, 1L5G) would be the external set, but they are not packaged here and would have to be assembled from scratch.

honest_claim_h3: No honest modelling claim can be made from this paper, because it releases a web tool and a 324-entry chemical building-block library rather than any set of measurements with an outcome attached.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a peptide's written sequence to predict how accurate a fast computer-built 3D model of it will be.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would train on peptide sequences in line notation paired with a quality score for the tool's quickly generated 3D model. This paper supplies no such pairs; I verified only three worked examples in the text.
plain_idea.predict: The output would be the deviation, in angstroms, between the fast-generated 3D model and an experimentally determined structure (from X-ray crystallography or nuclear magnetic resonance, deposited in the Protein Data Bank). Those reference structures are not provided here.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Peptide chemists currently run expensive molecular-dynamics refinement on every generated model; knowing in advance which ones are already close enough would save that compute. But the data to learn it has to come from elsewhere, not from this paper.

more_or_better_data.why: This paper contributes no data at all: a 324-entry monomer library and three case studies, against CREMP's 36,198 macrocyclic peptides with roughly 31.3 million conformers.

confidence_score.why: There are no replicate measurements and no per-example error estimates, so nothing here supports calibrated per-prediction confidence.

models_beatable.why: The paper's own generator is rule-based distance geometry (RDKit ETKDGv3) and is clearly less accurate than AlphaFold2-based HighFold or CREMP-trained diffusion models, but beating it is not a result anyone needs since those better tools already exist and are published (2024-2025).

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first condition: there is no feature/label table here to be our training set, so there is no shared split on which our model could see everything the baseline sees plus more.

ml_idea: None viable from this paper. The nearest idea - predicting which peptides a fast geometry-based builder already models well, so that expensive refinement can be skipped - would have to be built on CREMP (conformer ensembles for 36,198 macrocyclic peptides) plus PDB structures, using PEP-EDIT/pyPept merely as a utility for assembling molecules from line notation.

effort.compute_note: No estimate is meaningful because there is no dataset; the figures given reflect only the few megabytes of web assets and supplementary PDF I actually fetched.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the data availability statement and try one bulk download: it names only the interactive web server, and the monomer-library endpoint returns 404. That single check kills it in two minutes.

verdict_reason: This is a software/web-server paper with no released dataset. Part A fails at A1 (nothing downloadable: the data availability statement names only the interactive site, its monomer endpoint returns 404, and the source repository demands a login), at A2 (no prediction target exists; any label would have to be constructed by running the tool and matching outputs to PDB structures), at A5 (324 monomers and three validation case studies) and at A8 (the only candidate label is the tool's own geometric output). Separately, the task it does touch - 3D structure generation for cyclic and non-canonical peptides - is already served by HighFold, AlphaFold2-based cyclic predictors and CREMP-trained diffusion models, so even the derived project belongs to those datasets rather than this paper.
